newsitem.title: USA: Military helicopter crashes in Dallas, no survivors.
newsitem.headline: Military helicopter crashes in Dallas, no survivors.

text.p: A U.S.military helicopter crashed and burst into flames near a southeast Dallas school on Friday and officials said there were no signs of survivors.
Witnesses and police said the Marine Corp CH-53 helicopter narrowly missed at least one house as it went out of control and crashed into a field in the Dallas suburb of Hutchins.
"From the extent of damage, it is clear there is no chance of any survivors," police spokesman Ed Spencer said.
A Navy spokesman said CH-53 helicopters usually carry a crew of three or four. He said the helicopter was probably on training maneuvers when it crashed at around 6:00 p.m. EDT (2200 GMT).
Local residents reported hearing explosions seconds after the helicopter crashed.
"The fire was so intense, no survivors could be discerned," police Lt. Charles Epperson said.
Fire teams raced to the scene and put out the blaze as police sealed off the area less than one mile (1.6 km) from the intersection of two major highways.
Witnesses said the helicopter almost slammed into a house as it came down and credited the pilot with preventing a disaster.
"It was right over the house so whoever was piloting it is a hero in my books because he could have killed us all," local resident Velva Washburn said.
It was not immediately clear where the helicopter was based although the U.S. Naval Air Station in Dallas is only about 15 miles (24 km) from the crash site.
